candidates.computation_change_reason: Mercury MQL switches between 0.005 and 0.0005 µg/l depending on whether Part I requires Method 1631; resolving that permit condition changes the applicable numeric threshold (A), whether Method 1631 monitoring is required (B), and how mercury non-detects or missing results below the applicable MQL are classified (C).

Pollutant-specific MQL entries establish parameter-level numeric values; if MQL is treated as the compliance comparison point, the assigned value (here 50 µg/l versus 10 µg/l for many neighboring pollutants) changes whether a reported measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

Pesticide-category MQL values use a different numeric scale (e.g., 0.01 µg/l) than many base/neutral entries; interpreting this table as supplying enforceable limits would change compliance comparisons for pesticide parameters relative to base/neutral parameters.

The PCB MQL of 0.2 µg/l is an order of magnitude higher than several other pesticide entries; whether PCBs are in the monitored/applicable set and which numeric threshold applies depends on reading this row as operative for PCB discharges.
